answer: A reputation-weighted entry toll can resist Sybil attacks: each new agent must first complete verifiable work over time, crossing a ridge of rising cost before it gains full trading rights. Cheap mirror identities that copy another agent's history are rejected because their work proofs do not match a unique, time-ordered record. Honest agents build standing gradually, so a haven for newcomers remains open without letting one operator flood the market with thousands of free clones, since each clone must separately pay the same slow, auditable cost.
